cards.title: Test copy letters like ads before sending at scale
cards.summary: Write and test multiple letters as you would ads; a letter reaching a half-sold prospect can either complete the sale or forfeit the impression.
cards.use_when: Designing follow-up emails, direct mail or outreach to prospects and previous buyers for an ecommerce list.

cards.title: Eliminate costs that don't produce measurable sales
cards.summary: Weigh every project and method against a known cost per result, because small economies are irrelevant next to basic appeals that can halve or multiply results.
cards.use_when: Auditing any campaign spend — dealer allowances, displays, samples, art, media — and deciding where to cut or reallocate budget.

cards.title: Test letters and follow-ups with actual returns before full send
cards.summary: Keyed split tests across many letter variants pick the winner that gets the most responses, mirroring scientific ad testing.
cards.use_when: Running an email or direct-mail campaign (abandoned cart, replenishment reminder, win-back) and deciding which message to scale.

cards.title: Follow up inquirers along the original interest, not a new argument
cards.summary: A follow-up letter should complete the impression the prospect already formed, not restart with a different pitch.
cards.use_when: Writing follow-up emails to leads who requested a quote, sample, catalog, or signed up but did not buy.

cards.title: Give a compelling personal reason to order from you rather than a competitor's catalog
cards.summary: A gift or personal note enclosed with the catalog gives the buyer a reason to order from this vendor instead of the several competitors he also requested.
cards.use_when: Fulfilling catalog or sample requests in a category where buyers request multiple competing catalogs.

cards.title: Price prompt action into your offer rather than losing to delay
cards.summary: You can afford to pay for immediate action; delay costs more than the inducement.
cards.use_when: Setting promotional mechanics (expiry windows, premiums, bundles) for a product launch or seasonal push.

cards.title: Choose product names that either tell a selling story or accept a long earned-meaning path
cards.summary: A name displayed prominently should aid advertising; descriptive names do, meaningless coined names only pay off after long advertising.
cards.use_when: Naming a new product, bundle, or house brand where the name will be displayed in ads and on listings.

cards.title: When a common name is unavoidable, use the founder's name
cards.summary: A man's name as an auxiliary brand is better than a coined name because it signals personal pride in the product.
cards.use_when: Naming a product whose category term must be a common name (e.g., you must call it 'soap' or 'oil').

cards.title: Eliminate wasted ad display space telling no selling story
cards.summary: A vast amount of space is wasted displaying names and pictures that tell no selling story; modern advertising moves to cut that waste.
cards.use_when: Auditing ad creative or PDP hero modules where brand marks, logos, or decorative images occupy prime real estate.

cards.title: Key every ad so results can be known and proved
cards.summary: Ads that are unkeyed are spent blindly; the source argues you can prove an unprofitable ad's worthlessness with a simple keyed test.
cards.use_when: Setting up spend for any paid channel, landing page, or campaign where you cannot yet say whether it pays.

cards.title: Judge ads by traced returns, not by whether you personally like them
cards.summary: Ads that look crowded or verbose to an admirer may be the top payers; the type with the best traced performance is the one to run.
cards.use_when: Deciding which creative or page style to scale when stakeholders have aesthetic preferences.

cards.title: Apply the storekeeper's discipline to national-scale spend
cards.summary: A storekeeper charges every line of an ad to a department and every inch must justify its cost next day; most national advertising is done without that justification.
cards.use_when: Allocating budget across product lines, departments, or channels where spend is currently credited only by overall business growth.

cards.title: Treat advertising as a gamble to be removed, not a tonic to endorse
cards.summary: Spending because advertising worked for others is like taking a secret tonic on endorsement; if the business thrives, the tonic gets credit regardless.
cards.use_when: Evaluating whether to launch or continue a paid channel because competitors or past results suggest it 'must' work.

cards.title: Win on a small scale before running on a large scale
cards.summary: Ads based on known statistics were keyed at the start and proved themselves at small scale before big rollout.
cards.use_when: Planning a product launch or campaign scale-up where you want evidence before committing large circulation or spend.

cards.title: Test follow-up sequences because they complete or forfeit the sale
cards.summary: Letters to inquirers and follow-up letters show the same differences as ads — some get action, some complete a sale, some forfeit the impression gained.
cards.use_when: Designing post-inquiry sequences (samples, quotes, cart abandonment) where the first contact only half-converted the buyer.

cards.title: Match offer mechanics to the line, but keep the universal principles
cards.summary: Ways of getting action are many and rarely transfer directly between lines, but the underlying principles are universal.
cards.use_when: Adapting a proven promotion, premium, or urgency tactic from another category to your own product.

cards.title: Choose the right TikTok ad format for each objective
cards.summary: Match in-feed, Spark Ads, search ads, and Shop ads to distinct ecommerce goals instead of defaulting to one format.
cards.use_when: Planning which TikTok ad type to build for a launch, a scaling push, a demand-capture play, or a native checkout offer.

cards.title: Set TikTok budgets to clear the learning phase
cards.summary: Configure daily ad-set budgets as a multiple of target CPA to gather ~25 conversions in 7 days before judging results.
cards.use_when: Setting launch budgets and ROAS targets for a new TikTok campaign or ad set for an ecommerce product.

cards.title: Set up a TikTok Ads account for approval and safety
cards.summary: Complete the business, payment, audience, and brand-safety settings that keep a TikTok ad account deliverable and unbanned.
cards.use_when: Opening or hardening a TikTok ad account before spending on ecommerce campaigns.

cards.title: Set up a TikTok Business Center and link all assets
cards.summary: Centralize users, ad accounts, organic accounts, pixels, catalogs, and shops in one Business Center for scalable access control.
cards.use_when: Managing an ecommerce brand's TikTok advertising with agencies, contractors, or multiple accounts and shops.

cards.title: Install and verify the TikTok pixel before spending
cards.summary: Deploy the TikTok pixel with maximum data sharing and confirm events fire so campaigns can optimize toward purchase.
cards.use_when: Preparing a store to run TikTok ads optimized for add-to-cart or purchase events.

cards.title: Build a pain-solution ad with the 8-step structure
cards.summary: Sequence hook, problem, failed solution, product intro, feature-benefits, demo, desired result, and CTA in a TikTok ad.
cards.use_when: Writing a TikTok product ad for a problem-solving product (e.g., a foot-support or pain-relief item) that needs a clear narrative.

cards.title: Open ads with a curiosity gap
cards.summary: Use story, visual, or expectation-gap hooks so viewers must keep watching to resolve incomplete information.
cards.use_when: Writing the first three seconds of a TikTok ad when retention is the main problem.

cards.title: Use pattern interrupts to beat the scroll reflex
cards.summary: Break the brain's prediction of 'normal content' with a visually unexpected opening before showing the product.
cards.use_when: Producing the opening shot of a TikTok ad when the video looks too much like everything else in the feed.

cards.title: Apply authority bias in product ads
cards.summary: Borrow credibility visually or verbally — expert attire, first-person credentials, or a known face — so viewers trust the claim.
cards.use_when: Casting or scripting a TikTok ad for a product where trust is the conversion barrier (supplements, health, technical goods).

cards.title: Align ads with the buyer's identity
cards.summary: Write and cast ads that call out the identity the customer wants to occupy, not just the product's features.
cards.use_when: Positioning a TikTok ad for a lifestyle, wellness, hobby, or premium product where self-image drives purchase.

cards.title: Anchor price against a higher reference
cards.summary: Show a higher price or prior cost first, then your actual price, so the real price feels like a gain.
cards.use_when: Writing a TikTok ad or PDP creative for a value-focused or premium product where price is the objection.

cards.title: Build reciprocity with tutorial-style ads
cards.summary: Teach something genuinely useful before pitching so viewers feel compelled to give back by buying.
cards.use_when: Planning long-form or educational TikTok ad content for a considered-purchase product.

cards.title: Use scarcity and social proof in TikTok creatives
cards.summary: Trigger FOMO with restock/stock messaging and borrow trust with reviews, real customers, and follower counts.
cards.use_when: Writing ads for products with demand spikes, waitlists, or strong review bases where proof drives conversion.

cards.title: Judge TikTok demand before committing budget
cards.summary: Weigh audience breadth, time spent, and social-commerce growth to decide how much to invest in TikTok for your store.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to open a TikTok acquisition channel at all, or how to justify the channel to a skeptical team.

cards.title: Back-in-stock scarcity ads and comment mining
cards.summary: Use sold-out/restock messaging and customer comment sections to build authentic scarcity creative for ecommerce brands.
cards.use_when: Planning acquisition creative for a product that has sold out or restocked, or when you need low-cost ad concepts that signal real demand.

cards.title: Stack social proof in the first seconds of ad creative
cards.summary: Layer reviews, real-customer footage and follower counts into ads to lift credibility and performance.
cards.use_when: Producing ad creative for a PDP-driven campaign where you need higher trust and click-through on cold audiences.

cards.title: Specificity principle for claim writing
cards.summary: Replace vague benefit claims with precise numbers, timeframes and percentages to make ad copy and PDP claims believable.
cards.use_when: Writing ad hooks, PDP headlines, bullets or email subject lines where claims currently sound generic and are being ignored.

cards.title: Using TikTok Creative Center top ads for swipe files
cards.summary: Search and filter TikTok's free ads library to collect hook and format inspiration, while accounting for opt-in limitations.
cards.use_when: Sourcing ad inspiration or competitor research before shooting a new batch of TikTok creatives for your product category.

cards.title: TikTok One top ads insight for category creative angles
cards.summary: Use TikTok One's creative library and top-ads insight panel to extract category-level selling points and audience angles.
cards.use_when: Deciding which creative angles and selling points to test for a category (e.g. beauty, personal care) on TikTok Shop.

cards.title: Organized ad swipe files with a paid ad-spy tool
cards.summary: Build boards of competitor and category ads with a paid library that captures opted-out ads and offers strong search.
cards.use_when: Running frequent creative testing and needing a persistent, searchable swipe file across TikTok and other platforms, including competitor accounts.

cards.title: TikTok Shop product research with Kalodata
cards.summary: Use TikTok Shop sales data to find and validate products before committing to ad spend.
cards.use_when: Selecting which product to launch or source for a TikTok Shop store, before building creative or landing pages.

cards.title: Three ad production options: DIY, UGC creators, AI
cards.summary: Compare the cost, speed, scalability and conversion trade-offs of in-house, creator and AI-produced TikTok ads.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to resource a new batch of TikTok ad creative when you have limited budget and time.

cards.title: Script and shoot a problem-solution ad yourself
cards.summary: Write a UGC-style script and film it in segments on a phone for fast, low-cost ad testing.
cards.use_when: Producing first-party ad creative for a product demo when budget doesn't allow creators.

cards.title: CapCut assembly workflow for TikTok ads
cards.summary: Cut dead space, enhance audio, add text, sound effects, music and captions to assemble a vertical ad in CapCut.
cards.use_when: Editing a filmed or AI-generated ad for TikTok to meet platform pacing and accessibility norms.

cards.title: Add B-roll to hold attention in short-form ads
cards.summary: Overlay supporting footage on top of talking-head segments to keep viewers watching and illustrate claims.
cards.use_when: Editing a talking-head ad that risks losing viewers during explanation or demo segments.

cards.title: Hiring UGC creators through marketplaces
cards.summary: Brief and buy creator ad packages that test multiple hooks, using marketplaces with transparent pricing.
cards.use_when: Scaling creative volume after an angle works, or when you don't want to appear on camera yourself.

cards.title: Generate AI talking-actor ads with emotion tagging
cards.summary: Create AI spokesperson videos in Arc Ads with script, actor selection, emotion prompts and model choice.
cards.use_when: Producing a high volume of talking-head ad variants fast, when real creators are too slow or expensive.

cards.title: AI fashion try-on ads from product photos
cards.summary: Generate realistic model try-on videos from a clothing product image using Arc Ads presets.
cards.use_when: Selling apparel and needing model footage in many styles or scenes without booking shoots.

cards.title: AI product-showcase ads with actor holding your SKU
cards.summary: Generate AI actor videos holding or using a physical product from a clean product image plus a written direction.
cards.use_when: Advertising a physical product that isn't apparel and you need demonstration footage without a shoot.

cards.title: AI video ad generation: aspect ratio, prompt description, extensions
cards.summary: How to generate a UGC-style talking-head video ad with an AI video tool, including prompt structure and extending a cut-off clip.
cards.use_when: You need a first batch of paid-social ad creatives (TikTok/Meta feed) for a product page or offer and are generating them with an AI avatar tool rather than shooting.

cards.title: Swipe competitor hooks and re-voice them for your product
cards.summary: Download a winning competitor or platform hook, upload it to an AI ad tool, and regenerate it with your product inserted to test hook variations cheaply.
cards.use_when: You have product and offer ready but are stuck on ad angles, or you want to test multiple opening hooks for the same PDP/offer without reshooting.

cards.title: Choose the right AI video model for your ad by constraint
cards.summary: Model selection for AI ad video: pick based on which constraint matters most — realism, exact length, or resolution.
cards.use_when: You are generating product or UGC-style ad videos and need to decide which generation model to spend credits on for a given spot length or placement.

cards.title: Motion control and presets to skip
cards.summary: Use motion-transfer to animate a still of a person/product into an existing motion, and avoid the unboxing POV preset because of hand artifacts.
cards.use_when: You want a scroll-stopping format (person reactivating a product, showing a device in motion) without a shoot, or you are deciding which AI presets are worth spending credits on.

cards.title: Pick the TikTok ad objective that matches your goal (and why Sales is the default)
cards.summary: TikTok campaign objectives map to funnel stages, but optimizing for Sales is the source's default because it trains delivery toward purchases.
cards.use_when: You are setting up a new TikTok Ads Manager campaign for a product and need to decide what to optimize the account toward before spending budget.

cards.title: Manual vs Smart+ campaign and the product catalog setting
cards.summary: Choose manual for control, disable the campaign catalog to avoid showing unintended products under your video, and label campaigns by audience for later reporting.
cards.use_when: You are configuring a new TikTok Sales campaign and deciding whether to use Smart+, whether to show a product catalog under the video, and how to name campaigns.

cards.title: Campaign budget optimization: off for testing, on for scaling
cards.summary: Leave CBO off when testing audiences so each ad group gets a defined budget, then enable it when scaling to let TikTok allocate toward what already works.
cards.use_when: You are deciding between campaign-level and ad-group-level budget allocation for a TikTok campaign, particularly when comparing broad vs interest audiences.

cards.title: Budget recommendations for TikTok: CPA multiples vs TikTok's 10x rule
cards.summary: TikTok recommends 10x CPA daily budget; the source prefers 2x current CPA (or $50 if unknown, $20 minimum) and frames budgets around escaping the learning phase.
cards.use_when: You are deciding how much daily budget to put behind a new TikTok conversion campaign for a product.

cards.title: TikTok cost expectations and the one lever that moves them
cards.summary: Typical TikTok cost ranges (CPM, CPC, CPV) and the factors that shift them, with creative quality named as the dominant driver.
cards.use_when: You are setting CPA and ROAS targets for a TikTok ad plan or diagnosing why your costs are above/below plan.

cards.title: Audience targeting: start broad, layer interest testing later
cards.summary: Broad targeting is the source's default because the algorithm finds buyers; add interest/behavior ad groups only when budget allows a clean comparison.
cards.use_when: You are configuring TikTok ad-group targeting (demographics, interests, spending power, devices) for a product campaign.

cards.title: Build one ad group, then duplicate it for multiple audiences
cards.summary: Set up one ad group with all creatives first, then duplicate the ad group to create audience variants rather than rebuilding ads each time.
cards.use_when: You are structuring a TikTok campaign that needs separate broad and interest (or demographic) ad groups using the same creative set.

cards.title: Set up TikTok in-feed ad creative: CTA, music, and the ad-library checkbox
cards.summary: Practical creative-level settings for a TikTok ad: use multiple CTAs for testing, decide on music sharing, and uncheck the ad-library box.
cards.use_when: You are in the ad creative step of a TikTok campaign, uploading a video or spark post, and setting the CTA, URL, and visibility options.

cards.title: Keyword research for TikTok search ads with the Keyword Planner
cards.summary: Use TikTok's Keyword Planner to build a 20–50 keyword list filtered by competition and volume, then save it as a plan to upload into a search campaign.
cards.use_when: You want to run TikTok search ads (users typing queries inside TikTok) for a product and need a keyword list with realistic CPC and volume expectations.

cards.title: Build a TikTok search campaign and pick match types
cards.summary: Set up a TikTok search campaign from a saved keyword plan, choose phrase match as the middle ground, and disable automated keywords.
cards.use_when: You are launching a TikTok search ad campaign targeting people actively searching for your product terms.

cards.title: Mine the search term report and add negative keywords
cards.summary: After launching a search campaign, review the search terms your ads actually appeared for and exclude unwanted queries with negative keywords.
cards.use_when: You have a TikTok search campaign running and need to protect spend from irrelevant queries that don't match product intent.

cards.title: Spark ads: requirements and the organic-first six-step workflow
cards.summary: Run Spark ads by posting creative organically first, waiting 5–7 days to prove it, then amplifying the winners with paid budget.
cards.use_when: You want to amplify organic TikTok content (your own or a creator's) as a paid ad rather than treating paid and organic as separate tracks.

cards.title: Test TikTok creative organically before spending ad budget
cards.summary: Run a six-step Spark Ads loop that posts videos organically first, waits 5-7 days for full organic reach, then amplifies only the proven winners with paid budget.
cards.use_when: You are planning TikTok acquisition creative for a store and deciding which videos deserve paid spend versus which should be left to run free.

cards.title: Set up a Spark Ad from your own organic post
cards.summary: Inside Ads Manager's ad creative step, select TikTok post to run an existing organic video as a Spark Ad from your own account.
cards.use_when: You have an organic TikTok post from your own profile that performed well and you want to put paid amplification behind it.

cards.title: Run an influencer's video as a Spark Ad using an ad authorization code
cards.summary: Request a TikTok post code from the creator, then add it via 'add post' in the ad creative step to run their video as a paid ad from their profile.
cards.use_when: An influencer posted a video with your product and you want to amplify it with paid spend as a Spark Ad from their handle.

cards.title: Why Spark Ads engagement accrues to the organic post
cards.summary: Likes, comments and engagement on a Spark Ad also appear on the original organic post, creating one amplified asset rather than a separate ad unit.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether to run creator content as a Spark Ad versus a standalone ad creative, and want to understand the compounding effect on the original post.

cards.title: Stand up the TikTok Shop accounts needed before running Shop ads
cards.summary: Running TikTok Shop / GMV Max ads requires a Seller Center, a linked Business Center and Ads Manager, plus GMV Max authorization and admin access to the shop.
cards.use_when: You are preparing an ecommerce store to sell directly inside TikTok and need to know which accounts and permissions must exist before launch.

cards.title: Sync your Shopify catalog into TikTok Shop
cards.summary: Install the official TikTok app for Shopify to sync products, stock and pricing into your Seller Center instead of creating listings by hand.
cards.use_when: You are launching a TikTok Shop and want product listings, pricing and stock to flow from your existing ecommerce catalog rather than manual entry.

cards.title: Read the Seller Center dashboard and fix listings below good quality
cards.summary: The Seller Center home, products and marketing tabs surface orders, violations, low stock and listing quality issues you must resolve to sell effectively.
cards.use_when: You are operating a live TikTok Shop and need a routine for catching operational and listing problems before they cost sales.

cards.title: Structure open and target affiliate collaborations with commission tiers
cards.summary: Offer open collaborations at a fixed commission to anyone who drives a sale, and send target collaborations with custom rates to handpicked creators.
cards.use_when: You want to recruit TikTok creators to post tagged videos for your products without paying upfront for content that doesn't sell.

cards.title: Set up a GMV Max campaign that sells inside TikTok
cards.summary: GMV Max runs a single campaign that tests all tagged product videos, optimizes against a target product ROI, and checks buyers out inside TikTok.
cards.use_when: You have a TikTok Shop with tagged creator videos and want paid distribution that drives direct in-app purchases.

cards.title: Monitor GMV Max creative performance and boost winning ads
cards.summary: Use GMV Max analytics and the creatives view to see which videos are delivering, and apply a creative boost to push extra daily budget behind winners.
cards.use_when: Your GMV Max campaign is live and you need to see which tagged videos are actually running and where to add incremental spend.

cards.title: Build retargeting audiences from website, engagement and shop activity
cards.summary: Use TikTok's audience manager to build custom audiences from pixel events, video engagement and TikTok Shop activity, then exclude purchasers to avoid wasted spend.
cards.use_when: You want to run TikTok remarketing to store visitors, content engagers or shop visitors and need to define the right audience rules.

cards.title: Run TikTok retargeting campaigns with budget-tiered audience structure
cards.summary: Apply the retargeting audiences in a sales campaign via manual targeting, and scale the number of retargeting and re-engagement campaigns as budget grows.
cards.use_when: You have built TikTok retargeting audiences and want a campaign structure that matches your monthly ad budget.

cards.title: Audit Performance Max Spend Distribution Before Replacing It
cards.summary: Break down where PMax actually spends your budget — roughly 60-70% Shopping, 20-30% search text, 5-10% image/video retargeting — to see which components you can rebuild with better control.
cards.use_when: When deciding whether to keep leaning on Performance Max or to build manual campaign structures, and you need evidence of what PMax is doing with the budget.

cards.title: Performance-Based Shopping Structure by ROAS Tiers
cards.summary: Segment Standard Shopping products into four ROAS/spend tiers when product margins are similar, so budget flows to proven winners, zombies get tested, and inefficient spend is cut.
cards.use_when: Setting up or restructuring Standard Shopping campaigns for a store where product-level profit margins are within about 10% of each other.

cards.title: Gross Profit Margin Shopping Structure When Margins Vary
cards.summary: When product margins differ widely, build Shopping campaigns around margin tiers and set lower ROAS targets on high-margin items and higher targets on low-margin items to stay profitable at scale.
cards.use_when: Structuring Standard Shopping campaigns for a catalog where product-level margins vary significantly (the source cites roughly 30% to 70% as an example range).

cards.title: Shopping Feed Optimization: Titles, Images, Budget Priority
cards.summary: Beyond campaign structure, optimize keyword-rich product titles, high-quality images, and give Shopping the largest share of your Google Ads budget since it is the core ecommerce placement.
cards.use_when: Improving Standard Shopping campaign performance for a store — particularly product feed quality and cross-campaign budget allocation.

cards.title: Separate Brand and Non-Brand Search Campaigns
cards.summary: Split branded and non-branded search traffic into distinct campaigns so you can see true incremental performance and set brand ROAS targets much higher than non-brand targets.
cards.use_when: Restructuring Google Search campaigns to reveal true incremental acquisition and avoid PMax's tendency to over-index on branded traffic.

cards.title: Use Fewer Headlines and Descriptions to Speed Ad Testing
cards.summary: Limit responsive search ad assets to roughly 8 headlines and 2 descriptions instead of Google's maximum, so each combination accumulates enough impressions to actually be tested.
cards.use_when: Writing or revising responsive search ad copy and wanting interpretable test results rather than an untested combinatorial sprawl.

cards.title: Build Single-Themed Ad Groups from Keyword and PMax Search-Term Research
cards.summary: Mine the PMax search terms report plus Keyword Planner for proven queries, then organize keywords into single-themed ad groups with matching ad copy to raise relevance and quality score.
cards.use_when: Structuring Search campaigns and writing ad copy after deciding to move search traffic out of PMax.
